column1: # THE SECTOR ROWS (2026-09-30): the record ruler of a sector channel, read from Ken French's
# value-weighted monthly industry portfolios (10 and 49 industries) beside the market (Mkt-RF + RF)
# and the bill rate, 1926-07 to 2026-08 (CRSP vintage 202608). Generator: `record_bands -sectors
# publishes them (unzipped; the first monthly block of each, -99.99 a missing month). Every value
# reproduced to six decimals by an independent implementation of the same definitions.
# momentum   each month, industries ranked by their cumulative return over the `form` months ending
#            two months back (12-1: eleven months; 6-1: five) in excess of the market's over the same
#            months, an industry dropped from the month when any window month or the held month is
#            blank; long the top 3 of 10 (10 of 49), short the bottom 3 (10), equal-weighted, held
#            one month. `mean spread` is the mean monthly long-minus-short return; the band its 5th
#            and 95th percentile over 12-month block resamples of the spread series. `post-1963`
# trend      per industry, the mean next-month return in excess of the bill rate after a positive
#            signal minus after a negative one, averaged over the industries; `12m`: the trailing
#            twelve months' return over the bill rate's, `sma10`: the price index above its ten-month
#            mean, both read at the end of the month before. The band resamples the held months in
#            12-month blocks and recomputes the per-industry statistic.
# shape      the mean over months of the cross-sectional sd of the industries' returns; the median
#            pairwise correlation over the whole sample, over the months at or under the market's
#            10th percentile and over those strictly between its 45th and 55th; a pair counts with
#            The market's monthly sd over the same months is printed beside them: the scale the
#            cross-sectional sd is graded against, so a world of another volatility reads the
# Returns and spreads are monthly simple returns as fractions. The world is graded on the
# 10-industry rows once a sector channel exists; the 49-industry rows are the record's own.
